items.rawSummary: Washington, D.C. saw a burst of Supreme Court decisions on presidential power, Federal Reserve independence, and mail-in balloting, alongside a U.S.-Iran ceasefire agreement, a federal probe into a businessman, and President Trump’s sharp reactions to the court’s ballot ruling and falling oil prices.
items.analysis: The U.S. and Iran agreed to halt attacks and meet this week, according to Axios, sending stock futures higher; the White House confirmed it is upholding the ceasefire, responding to attacks on commercial vessels, and warning that violence will be met with violence. Secretary Rubio and envoy Witkoff are set to brief Congress on Iran. Meanwhile, U.S.-Israel relations have cooled under the Trump administration’s ‘America First’ approach, with Vice President Vance cautioning Israel against alienating the U.S., and former Secretary Kerry blaming the president’s dismissive handling of Netanyahu’s war briefing for setting a path to conflict. The U.S. also reimposed sanctions on Russian oil exports after waivers lapsed. On the economic front, President Trump noted that WTI crude fell to $69 per barrel and urged consumers to report retail price abuses. In legal and investigative spheres, a Belgium-based foundation filed a Justice Department complaint accusing Israeli Minister Ben-Gvir of overseeing systematic torture and killings of Palestinians, including U.S. citizens, while a federal grand jury probes businessman Neville Roy Singham over alleged money laundering and funding of left-wing groups, including pro-Hamas entities and Code Pink. The Supreme Court issued significant rulings: expanding the president’s power to fire top officials, which President Trump hailed as a historic ruling in the ‘Slaughter Case’ confirming his Article II authority to remove executive branch officers; in a separate 5-4 decision, the court blocked the removal of Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook while litigation continues; and it declined to hear Trump’s appeal of the $5 million judgment for sexually abusing and defaming E. Jean Carroll. In a 5-4 decision written by Justice Barrett, the court also upheld state laws allowing mail-in ballots received after Election Day if postmarked by Election Day, rejecting a Republican-backed challenge supported by Trump; the ruling preserves current voting rules in over half the states ahead of the 2026 midterms. President Trump denounced the mail-in ballot ruling as a ‘tremendous loss’ and urged Senate Republicans to pass the Save America Act. A prediction market now shows a 62% chance of Trump’s impeachment before January 2028.

items.title: Beijing, China: China defended its rare-earth export controls, stating they are a justified measure to contain Japan's 'neo-militarism' and urging Tokyo to return to peaceful development.
items.description: China defended its rare-earth export controls, stating they are a justified measure to contain Japan's 'neo-militarism' and urging Tokyo to return to peaceful development.
items.rawSummary: Following a plane crash that struck its tallest building, Beijing is broadening a yuan-based oil trading system, advancing AI cybersecurity capabilities, reporting record submarine construction, and hosting Belarus's leader, while defending rare-earth export controls as a response to Japanese policy.
items.analysis: The crash of a Sunward SA60L light aircraft into Beijing’s CITIC Tower scattered debris and prompted an evacuation, with casualty figures still unconfirmed and questions arising about aviation safety over central districts. Separately, Beijing is expanding a yuan‑based financial architecture for international oil trades, which .com describes as providing Iran and Russia with a mechanism to circumvent Western sanctions. In technology, the Chinese AI model GLM‑5.2 from Z.ai surpassed Anthropic’s Claude Code on a vulnerability detection benchmark at one‑sixth the cost, signaling progress in cybersecurity. China has also reportedly built 24 submarines over the past five years, more than the United States and Russia combined, while Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko met with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing. Concurrently, Beijing defended its rare-earth export controls, arguing they are a justified response to Japan’s “neo-militarism” and urging Tokyo to return to peaceful development.

items.title: Doha, Qatar, Qatar: Axios reports that U.S. envoy Witkoff and Jared Kushner travel to Doha today and will meet with the Qatari Prime Minister on Tuesday; on Wednesday, U.S. and Iranian technical teams will meet separately with Qatari and Pakistani mediators.
items.description: Axios reports that U.S. envoy Witkoff and Jared Kushner travel to Doha today and will meet with the Qatari Prime Minister on Tuesday; on Wednesday, U.S. and Iranian technical teams will meet separately with Qatari and Pakistani mediators.
items.rawSummary: Qatar has suspended non-international maritime activity amid regional security tensions as U.S. and Iranian envoys prepare for a week of high-level and technical talks in Doha.
items.analysis: Qatar’s Ministry of Transport directed owners and operators of non-international maritime vessels—including leisure boats, fishing boats, and jet skis—to suspend all sailing and maritime activities until further notice, exempting ships subject to international maritime conventions, citing heightened security concerns in the region. The move extends earlier civilian maritime restrictions prompted by Iranian strikes near the Strait of Hormuz, where a Qatari citizen was killed and another injured after their vessel went missing during military operations. On the diplomatic front, Axios reported that U.S. Special Envoy Witkoff and Jared Kushner will travel to Doha today, meet with the Qatari Prime Minister on Tuesday, and that on Wednesday U.S. and Iranian technical teams will hold separate meetings with Qatari and Pakistani mediators—aligning with Iran’s earlier statement that no direct technical meetings with the U.S. are scheduled this week. Meanwhile, Iranian President Pezeshkian announced $6 billion of frozen assets held in Qatar would be released and claimed sanctions on oil and petrochemicals were lifted, details Washington has not corroborated. The White House confirmed the high-level talks, while also warning that President Trump retains the right to use military force and that violence will be met with violence, underscoring the fragile nature of the diplomatic track.

items.title: Seoul, South Korea: President Lee Jae Myung ordered a government investigation into the national football team's World Cup group-stage exit and questioned the coaching appointment; head coach Hong Myung-bo subsequently announced his resignation.
items.description: President Lee Jae Myung ordered a government investigation into the national football team's World Cup group-stage exit and questioned the coaching appointment; head coach Hong Myung-bo subsequently announced his resignation.
items.rawSummary: South Korea is navigating overlapping financial, political, and security developments as a stock market circuit breaker, a former first lady's bribery sentencing, and a new presidential probe into a World Cup exit coincide with record semiconductor gains and a large-scale drone-defense initiative.
items.analysis: The Korea Exchange triggered a circuit breaker on Thursday afternoon, halting trading after the benchmark index fell more than 8%; new data reveals the selloff was amplified by record margin loans now totaling around $26 billion, which doubled since early 2025. During the recent pullback, forced liquidation ratios spiked to 4–5% of total margin loans in a single day, well above the roughly 1% norm, as surging market capitalization had masked the absolute build-up in leverage. The sharp decline unfolded amid domestic political turbulence after former First Lady Kim Geun-hee was sentenced to seven years in prison on bribery charges, and that turbulence deepened on Saturday when President Lee Jae Myung ordered a government investigation into the national football team's World Cup group-stage exit, questioning the coaching appointment shortly before head coach Hong Myung-bo resigned. South Korean chipmakers SK Hynix and Samsung have nonetheless posted extraordinary year-to-date gains of 348% and 199% respectively, driving Asian semiconductor stocks to record levels against major US tech names, even as the so-called Magnificent Seven fell 14% this month. The market stress and political frictions coexist with a broader defense pivot, with South Korea unveiling plans this week to train 500,000 drone operators and deploy 60,000 unmanned systems by 2029.

items.rawSummary: Pakistan conducted overnight airstrikes in eastern Afghanistan targeting militants, with Afghan authorities reporting dozens of civilian casualties.
items.analysis: Pakistan announced that it carried out overnight airstrikes in eastern Afghanistan, describing the operation as aimed at militant groups. Afghan authorities contested the account, asserting that the strikes killed dozens of civilians. The cross-border incident adds to persistent friction between the two neighbors. Details on the location and scale of the reported civilian harm remain limited, and independent verification was not immediately available.

items.title: China, China: China's M2 money supply reaches a record ~240% of GDP, the highest among major economies, after surging over 500% in dollar terms since the 2008 financial crisis, while gold reserves have risen only about 100% over the same period.
items.description: China's M2 money supply reaches a record ~240% of GDP, the highest among major economies, after surging over 500% in dollar terms since the 2008 financial crisis, while gold reserves have risen only about 100% over the same period.
items.rawSummary: Strong gold import volumes and central bank purchases are unfolding alongside a surge in China's money supply, which has reached a record 240% of GDP, highlighting gold's appeal as a store of value amid rapid monetary expansion.
items.analysis: China imported 163 tonnes of gold in May, the largest monthly volume since March 2024 and the third consecutive month above 150 tonnes, pushing total imports in the first five months of 2026 to 692 tonnes, a 76% year-on-year increase. Retail demand for physical bullion bars and gold accumulation plans has been the primary driver, while the People's Bank of China added another 10 tonnes to official reserves in May, its 19th straight monthly purchase, bringing holdings to a record 2,331 tonnes. The sustained appetite comes against a backdrop of unprecedented monetary expansion: China's M2 money supply has surged to a record ~240% of GDP, the highest ratio among major economies and up 100 percentage points since the 2008 financial crisis, with M2 in dollar terms having risen over 500% in that period. By comparison, gold reserves and total foreign exchange reserves have increased far more modestly, by about 100% and 60% respectively. The divergence between money supply growth and reserve asset accumulation helps explain the robust official and private-sector demand for gold as a hedge against fiat currency expansion.
